conviction_note: The half is already public -- revenue $66.5m, adj EBITDA $19.3m and TPV $8.3bn were all pre-released in the 8 July 2026 trading update that took the stock down 32.19% -- so 23 September has almost no surprise capacity on the reported half and the only live line is whether FY26 guidance ($135-142m / $38-42m) is reiterated. Findings sum to +0.9; I emit +0.7, a visible 0.2 haircut, because my net read is positive while the sealed lean is -0.166 and the stock has run +6.55% over 20 days (+9% in the last two weeks) into a print that contains no new numbers. print_vs_bar_pct (+1.0) is larger than expected_move_pct because the fundamental read is mildly constructive -- a guide set 8 days after period end with actuals in hand, with an EBITDA leg implying only ~+4% H2 growth at the midpoint -- while the reaction function is not: Boku's last two September interims, both preceded by a July trading update that pre-announced the half in exactly this way, fell 3.08% and 1.75%. The right scale for this event type is ~2.0-2.4%, not the baseline's 3.16% proxy, which is the median of all nine events including two trading updates that moved 8.65% and -32.19%.

findings.finding: The entire first half was pre-released eleven weeks ago, so the interims carry almost no surprise capacity on the reported numbers -- and Boku's last two September interims, both preceded by a July trading update that pre-announced the half in exactly the same way, fell 3.08% (2024-09-24) and 1.75% (2025-09-30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line's own history: 2 of 2 prior interims down, -3.08% and -1.75%, mean -2.4%. Every large move this name has made came on a Trading Update (+8.65% 2025-07-24, -32.19% 2026-07-08) or on Full Year Results (+4.43%, +7.60%), never on interims. The 217-day UK median gap between scheduled releases is why: the trading update, not the interim, is where Boku's price-sensitive information lands.
findings.original_quote: H1 2026 revenues of approximately $66.5 million, representing approximately 11% growth compared to underlying H1 2025 revenues of $59.9 million; Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $19.3 million with a margin of approximately 29%; Total Payment Volume of approximately $8.3 billion, up approximately 12%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced and I have sized it accordingly -- this is the one finding here that AGREES with the sealed lean of -0.166 and with the +6.55% run-up, which is why it is cut to -0.6 rather than carrying the -2.4% mean of the two prior interims. What is not fully priced is the SCALE: the baseline's event_move_proxy of 3.16% is the median of all nine observed events and is dragged up by two trading updates at +8.65% and -32.19%. Conditioned on event type, this name's interims travel ~2.0-2.4%. Anyone sizing this print off the blended proxy is sizing it roughly 40% too wide.
findings.independence: Corroborated by the Notice of Interim Results (2026-09-04), which schedules the event but pre-releases nothing further: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/notice-of-interim-results/9756992 . Edison's note on the trading update says explicitly that it rebased 'pending better visibility when the company reports H126 results in September' -- i.e. the sell-side treats September as the visibility event, not a numbers event: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/rebasing-expectations-2/BM-3663/ (2026-07-08).

findings.finding: FY26 guidance was set on 8 July, eight days after the half closed and with H1 actuals in hand, and its EBITDA leg is soft: guide $38-42m less H1's $19.3m implies H2 adj EBITDA of $18.7-22.7m against a derived H2-25 of about $19.9m -- roughly -6% to +14%, midpoint ~+4%, on a business that grew adj EBITDA 36% in FY25. A second cut eleven weeks after a guide set on actuals is a much lower-probability event than the July cut was.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line that moves this stock and it moves it violently: the FY26 cut on 2026-07-08 took it -32.19% in one session, the largest move in the nine-event history by a factor of four. The two upside guidance-bearing prints, FY24 results (2025-03-18) and FY25 results (2026-03-17), gave +4.43% and +7.60%. So this line pays asymmetrically when it surprises, and a mere reiteration -- which is my base case -- is worth far less than either tail.
findings.original_quote: Total Group revenue increased to $128.8m (FY 2024: $99.3m) ... Adjusted EBITDA rose by 36% to $41.3 million ... Own cash grew by 28% to $102.9m, up from $80.2m at 31 December 2024
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and cut hard for it. Boku carries 8 analysts on $1.06m/day of turnover, which is the TOP of this stage's measured coverage band rather than the under-read $1-5m/5-7-analyst regime the thesis targets, so the sell-side has certainly built this bridge. What the wire copy carries is 'Boku cuts guidance, shares slump 33%'; what it does not carry is that the resulting H2 EBITDA ask is ~+4% at the midpoint with the low end below prior year. The residual edge is with the marginal AIM price-setter reading the headline, not with the eight analysts.
findings.independence: Different document, same direction: the 2026-07-08 trading update itself, which sets the guide and states the offsetting cost action -- https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/trading-update/9657188 . NOTE ON DOUBLE-COUNTING: this finding and finding 3 (director buying) both argue 'the bar is beatable' from two independent documents; they are deliberately sized as a pair totalling +1.2, not as two full-size findings. CAVEAT ON THE ARITHMETIC: the H2-25 EBITDA base of ~$19.9m is DERIVED, not disclosed. FY25 adj EBITDA of $41.3m is confirmed in the document above, but the company gives H1-25 on an 'underlying' basis ($18.4m) and the FY25 RNS separately notes 'approximately $3m from launch-phase pricing related to a single Digital Wallet connection in H1 2025'. Adding that back gives reported H1-25 EBITDA of ~$21.4m and H2-25 of ~$19.9m. There is roughly $3m of uncertainty in that base, which is why the revenue leg of the same bridge (+3.9% to +14.6% H2 growth, midpoint ~+9.3%) is NOT claimed as undemanding -- it asks H2 to repeat H1's growth rate while the merchant dual-sourcing and the ~$4m/yr suspended DCB connection annualise into the H2 base. Only the EBITDA leg is load-bearing here.

findings.finding: The CEO bought 106,000 shares at 95p on 8 July 2026 -- the day of the 32% crash and the same day he set the FY26 guide -- and the CFO bought 65,000 at 98.75p on 10 July; both are now roughly 25-28% in the money at 122p.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No directly comparable prior instance in the nine-event history -- these are the only post-warning PDMR purchases in the observed record, so this line has no reaction distribution of its own on this name. That is the main reason it is sized at +0.4 rather than higher.
findings.original_quote: Stuart Neal, Chief Executive Officer ... acquisition of 106,000 common shares at a price of 95 pence per share ... following this transaction his total shareholding is 925,195 common shares, representing 0.31% of the issued share capital
findings.why_not_priced: PDMR RNS are filed at 15:30 and 11:33 on days when the stock had just fallen 32%, and no wire service carried them -- the July coverage is uniformly 'Boku slumps 33%'. If this were priced, the stock would not have bottomed at 94.6p the same afternoon and taken ten weeks to recover to 122p. The amounts are small in absolute terms (~GBP 101k and ~GBP 64k) and that is exactly why it is sized at +0.4: it is a signal about management's own read of the guide they had just set, not a material transfer of ownership.
findings.independence: Corroborated by the CFO's separate filing two days later, a different PDMR on a different date: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/pdmr-dealing/9663458 (2026-07-10, Robert Whittick, 65,000 shares at 98.75p). Points the same way as finding 2 and is sized as part of that pair.

findings.finding: Richard Griffiths -- founder of The Evolution Group and ORA Capital, a long-standing UK small-cap investor -- went from below 3% to 3.07% on 17 August and then to 4.25% on 18 September, converting his entire 1.05% CFD position into physical stock and adding ~3.35m shares of net new exposure; the second notification hit the wire at 17:09 on Monday 21 September, two days before the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not previously observable on this name -- Griffiths crossed 3% for the first time on 2026-08-17, so there is no prior instance of him accumulating into a Boku print. What the tape shows on the one day his buying is datable is that on 2026-09-11 the stock rose 5.36% (112.0p -> 118.0p) on 2,685,524 shares, roughly 4.6x the recent median, and that single session is essentially the whole of the baseline's +6.55% 20-day run-up.
findings.original_quote: Richard Griffiths ... date on which threshold was crossed or reached: 18 September 2026 ... date of notification: 21 September 2026 ... Resulting situation: 12,143,844 voting rights, 4.25% ... Position of previous notification: 2.02% voting rights attached to shares, 1.05% through financial instruments, 3.07% total
findings.why_not_priced: A TR-1 filed at 17:09 on a Monday evening is the single least-read regulated disclosure in the UK market: no wire carries it, it has no headline, and this stage's own positioning anchor -- the FCA aggregated NET SHORT register -- is structurally blind to long accumulation by construction. If it were priced, the baseline's priced_lean_pct would not read the +6.55% run-up as a -0.328 negative, because that run-up is not diffuse anticipation of a good print: it is one identifiable buyer absorbing one identifiable seller. Moving from CFD to physical is the part that is hard to explain as trading -- it surrenders leverage and takes on settlement and voting, which is what a holder does when he intends to stay.
findings.independence: Different filer, same register, and it is the other side of the same transfer: BlackRock's reducing TR-1 of 2026-09-14 puts its threshold crossing on 2026-09-11, the exact session of the +5.36% move on 4.6x volume -- https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/holding-s-in-company/9771260 . Third, independent corroboration that the September re-rating was NOT the company's own bid: Boku's buyback DECELERATED across the rally, 148,571 shares over 20-26 Aug at ~113.9p, 90,488 over 3-9 Sep at ~111.77p, then only 50,000 over 10-16 Sep at 120.00p -- https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/transaction-in-own-shares/9777296 . NOTE: finding 5 is the opposite side of this same register and the two are netted, not summed independently.

findings.finding: BlackRock has filed three reducing TR-1s in two months -- 6.75%, then 6.37% on 11 August, then 5.87% on 11 September, about 1.48m shares between the last two notifications alone -- and still holds 5.87%, so a demonstrated, persistent seller is live into the highest-volume session of the half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable in the nine-event history. The one datable instance is 2026-09-11, when BlackRock crossed below 6% and the stock nonetheless rose 5.36% on 2.69m shares -- i.e. on the only day we can price this seller's flow, the supply was absorbed with the price UP. That is why this is -0.5 rather than larger.
findings.original_quote: BlackRock, Inc. ... date on which threshold was crossed or reached: 11 September 2026 ... Resulting situation: 5.49% voting rights attached to shares, 0.37% through financial instruments, 5.87% total ... Position of previous notification: 6.37%
findings.why_not_priced: Same structural reason as finding 4 -- TR-1s carry no headline and no wire, and the sealed positioning anchor reads only the short register. But the honest read is that this is the WEAKER half of the transfer and it is sized as such: BlackRock's reductions look like passive/quant rebalancing rather than informed selling, and Griffiths' ~3.35m shares of net buying exceeds the ~2.5m BlackRock has shed across both notifications. Filed as a separate finding because it resolves against a different counterparty, but netted against finding 4 rather than summed as an independent negative.
findings.independence: Same register, opposite direction to finding 4 -- explicitly netted with it (+0.8 and -0.5 for a net +0.3 of positioning), not counted twice. The prior leg is a separate document: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/boku-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3-144a--boku/holding-s-in-company/9718880 (2026-08-12, 6.75% -> 6.37%, crossing 2026-08-11).

outside_window.finding: Boku's buyback has slowed to 50,000 shares a week into the close period (from 148,571/week in late August) and the extended authority runs to 10% of issued shares, up to a further 8,000,000 shares, expiring only at the FY26 results in March 2027. Resumption at the post-August pace (~120-150k/week, roughly 15-20% of median daily volume) is a mechanical bid that restarts AFTER the 23 September close and therefore earns this ranking nothing.

The ~$4m annual run-rate DCB connection suspended by local authorities, and the merchant that moved to dual sourcing, are both H2-26/FY27 revenue questions. Restoration or replacement would be sourced at the FY26 results in March 2027 or the January 2027 trading update, not on 23 September.

lessons_applied: CORRECTED AN ERROR IN MY OWN LARGEST FINDING. 'A number you could not confirm in the document is not load-bearing' sent me to fetch the FY25 results RNS, whose figures I had only from a search snippet. Doing so broke my pre_lessons claim that H2-26 adj EBITDA was 'guided below prior-year H2 at every point of the range': that rested on an H2-25 base of $22.9m derived by subtracting the UNDERLYING H1-25 EBITDA ($18.4m) from reported FY25 ($41.3m), which double-subtracts the ~$3m of H1-25 launch-phase Digital Wallet pricing. The correct base is ~$19.9m and the correct read is -6% to +14%, midpoint ~+4%. Finding 2 cut from +1.5 to +0.8 and restated, with the residual ~$3m of uncertainty marked in the finding and the revenue leg explicitly dropped as non-load-bearing.

Cut finding 1 from -0.9 to -0.6 on 'positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with'. It is the only finding in the set that agrees with the sealed lean and the run-up, so most of the -2.4% mean of the two prior interims is already in the price.

Applied 'the UK's analogue of a German ad-hoc is an RNS trading update -- check before sizing anything on the quarter' directly. Checked, and the answer is total: the whole half was pre-released on 8 July. That is why reported_quarter carries no positive size anywhere in this set.

Applied the coverage-regime rule. analyst_band '8-13' with 8 analysts on $1.06m/day of turnover puts Boku ABOVE the under-read $1-5m/5-7-analyst band the thesis targets, so finding 2 was haircut for a sell-side that has certainly built the same bridge -- while finding 4 was NOT haircut, because analyst coverage does not read TR-1s.

Made the caveat reach the number, per 'the hunter's own caveat has to reach the number'. baseline_tension says my net cuts against the lean, so expected_move_pct (+0.7) sits a stated 0.2 below the finding sum (+0.9) rather than equalling it.

Moved two items OUT of findings into outside_window on 'keep findings inside the exit window': the post-close-period buyback resumption and the DCB/dual-sourcing recovery, neither of which resolves on 23 September.

Resolved the double-count the lessons file warns about, in two places: findings 2 and 3 argue one proposition from two documents and are sized as a pair (+1.2 total); findings 4 and 5 are two sides of one register and are netted (+0.3 total), with both relationships written into the independence fields rather than left for the sum to get wrong.
Widened the impact bands on 'the tail is intact, so do not size as if it were not' -- no European price limit, and this name has a 32% single-session move in its own nine-event record.

Did NOT raise the emitted number on 'understatement is the hunters' systematic error'. That rule says size on the name's own reaction distribution, and this name's interims distribution is ~2.0-2.4% absolute with both observations negative, so a +0.7 is already a meaningful fraction of the conditional scale rather than a timid one.
